conflict_topics: ventilation responsibility (who must run extractor / open window)
future household rule about ventilation after smelly cooking
dialogue_quality_notes: Agents provide concrete reasons: Agent B cites headaches; Agent A cites dish timing and guest.
Agent C performed a concrete cooperative action (moved drying rack) rather than just verbal assent.
Agent B repeatedly asks for a simple yes/no agreement across rounds, producing some repetition.
No party capitulates; practical mitigations (window/extractor) are accepted while normative responsibility remains contested.
evaluation.final_reason: Practical mitigations were enacted (laundry moved, window opened, extractor on), but the normative disagreement over who should be responsible for ventilation going forward and the stove-access timing were not agreed or settled by the end of the transcript.
position_change_notes: Agent A: softened practical stance — turned on extractor and accepted window open — but retained opposition to a blanket future rule (no change on normative position).
Agent B: remained consistent in pushing for a rule that whoever cooks ventilates; repeated the proposal but did not accept A's conditional refusal.
Agent C: changed behavior by moving the drying rack (from previously not consenting to someone else moving it to actively moving it), enabling ventilation.
Agent D: pressed for stove access and echoed Agent B's proposal but did not change any position.

round_scores.evidence: Agent B demanded Agent A accept a standing rule that cooks must ventilate; Agent A refused to accept a rule during the incident and insisted the rain-facing window remain closed while Agent C's laundry was exposed. Incompatible claims about ventilation responsibility and immediate ventilation are asserted and unresolved.

Agent C voluntarily moves the drying rack away from the window, removing the immediate obstacle that prevented opening the window (practical de-escalation). The normative dispute about who must handle ventilation and stove access remains unsettled.

Agent B physically opens the window and Agent A agrees to the window being opened and to keep the extractor on now; the immediate odour problem is mitigated. The normative rule about future ventilation and the stove-release timing remain unresolved.

Agent B asks whether Agent A's extractor commitment is a one-time action or a future rule; Agent A clarifies it's only this time and refuses a blanket rule unless responsibility is agreed. The core normative disagreement persists without new concessions.

Agent B renews the proposal that whoever cooks runs the extractor during and ~20 minutes after smelly cooking; Agent D presses Agent A on stove timing and supports the proposal. Pressure increases (coalition forming) but no agreement is reached.

Agent A repeats refusal to accept a blanket 20-minute rule while maintaining the extractor now; Agent B reiterates the proposal and adds that cooks should ask for help if they cannot run the extractor. The normative responsibility and future rule remain unsettled; stove remains in use for several more minutes.

substantive_insights: Tension separates immediate practical mitigation (open window, run extractor) from longer-term normative assignment of responsibility (who 'must' ventilate).
A third party (Agent C) removed a concrete obstacle (laundry) which enabled ventilation without forcing Agent A to concede the rule.
Agent A consistently prioritizes the timing/quality of the current dish and resists accepting a standing obligation created during an incident.
Agent B frames ventilation as the cook's responsibility and escalates to a binary request repeatedly; Agent D supports pressure for stove access and the proposed rule.
